html:
On 1 May 1979 Greenland gained home rule from Denmark, with its own parliament and government, the Naalakkersuisut, after a referendum that January. Greenland had stopped being a colony in 1953, when it became part of Denmark.

The home rule government took over schools, social affairs and the economy. Greenlandic became the main language of government. In 1982 voters chose to leave the European Community, which they did in 1985, mainly to control their fishing.

A wider Self-Government Act in 2009 recognised Greenlanders as a people with the right to independence and gave them control of mineral resources. Denmark still runs foreign policy and defence, including the Thule base. Independence is a lasting debate in Nuuk, as in Nunavut across the water.
sum: On 1 May 1979 Greenland gained home rule from Denmark, with its own parliament and government, the Naalakkersuisut, after a referendum that January. Greenland had stopped being a colony in 1953, when it became part of Denmark.
